overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any alleged improper deliberation via Facebook, text, email, or office hours, issued cautions only, and declined to review subcommittee texts not raised in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Member's public Facebook post on the proposed transportation fee, and a colleague's share of it, allegedly constituted deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Ms. Greenfield’s Facebook post, and Ms. Nassiff’s sharing of that post, were directed to the general public, and not to fellow Committee members, and therefore did not constitute improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Two members' 'likes' of a colleague's Facebook post allegedly amounted to deliberation between a quorum outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, we decline to find a violation of the Open Meeting Law in this instance where neither Ms. Sullivan nor Ms. Nassiff knew that the other had “liked” Ms. Greenfield’s post and there is no indication that Ms. Greenfield solicited or expected any response.

allegations.summary: Text messages among members on the transportation program allegedly constituted serial deliberation among a quorum outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the text messages reviewed by our office do not constitute deliberation because each was between less than a quorum of the Committee, concerned different issues, and did not communicate information, thoughts, ideas, opinions, or plans between or among a quorum of the Committee.

allegations.summary: Chair's email answering a member of the public, with a quorum copied, allegedly constituted deliberation outside a meeting.
Office hours, offered phone calls, and member-to-member contacts allegedly enabled serial deliberation by a quorum on the transportation changes.
allegations.key_passage: Considering the above, we find no evidence that a quorum of the Committee deliberated outside of a meeting, and we therefore find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Whether subcommittee text messages constituted improper quorum deliberation was raised in the review, though the complaint did not allege it.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was filed only with the Committee and did not allege improper deliberation between or among a quorum of any of the Committee’s subcommittees, we do not make a finding as to whether any of the text messages reviewed may have constituted improper deliberation between or among a quorum of a subcommittee.
